title: Evidence for a causal association between milk intake and cardiometabolic disease outcomes using a two-sample Mendelian Randomization analysis in up to 1,904,220 individuals
authors: Vimaleswaran KS, Zhou A, Cavadino A, Hyppönen E
population: 1958 British Birth Cohort, Health and Retirement Study and UK Biobank (417,236 individuals) with summary data from GIANT, Global Lipids, MAGIC, ICBP, DIAGRAM and CARDIoGRAM
funder: British Heart Foundation (D-CarDia collaboration, PG/09/023); National Health and Medical Research Council, Australia (1123603); Rank Prize Funds Nutrition Committee Travel Award; Medical Research Council (MR/S024778/1).
authorConflicts: The authors declare no competing interests.
result: The T allele of the LCT variant rs4988235, which indexes higher milk intake, was associated with higher BMI and lower total, LDL and HDL cholesterol. Per T allele: coronary artery disease OR 0.86 (95% CI 0.75 to 0.99; CARDIoGRAM, 22,233 cases and 64,762 controls); type 2 diabetes OR 1.06 (0.97 to 1.16; DIAGRAM, 34,840 cases) and 0.89 (0.82 to 0.97; UK Biobank, 20,820 cases).
